name: Selleasy
summary: Shopify upsell and cross-sell app (by Logbase): bundles and product add-ons on the product page, add-on pop-ups and response-based funnels on the cart, one-click post-purchase offers and thank-you page add-ons. Priced by your store's total order count rather than by upsell revenue, and free under 50 orders a month.
best_for: shopify stores that want bundles, add-ons, cart funnels and post-purchase offers out of one app and would rather be billed on order volume than hand over a share of the upsell revenue — and small stores in particular, since under 50 orders a month the full strategy set costs nothing
skip_if: you are on Shopify Plus and came for checkout upsells, or you want AI recommendations at any real volume: both start at Pro, $49 a month, which the App Store listing never shows — and a high-order store that runs no upsells still pays the top Starter step
honest_knock:
The meter is your whole store, not the app. Every Starter tier counts total store orders, so the free plan's 50-order ceiling is reached by any shop doing two orders a day whether or not a single upsell ever fired — and, read the other way, a 5,000-order store running one quiet bundle pays the top step of the ladder all the same. That cuts both ways and it is cheap in either direction, but it is not the meter most people assume they are signing up to.

Second, the App Store listing shows only the Starter ladder, so it reads as though $29 is the ceiling. It is not. Pro at $49 and Max at $99 exist only on logbase.io, and that is where AI recommendations at volume and checkout upsells for Shopify Plus sit — the two upgrades a growing store is most likely to want.

Third, every Starter tier says '50 free AI recommendations' with no period attached, while Pro says '1,000 AI recommendations/month' and Max says '2,500 AI recommendations/month'. The contrast in wording suggests the 50 is a one-off allowance rather than a monthly one, but neither page says so outright. Ask before you plan around it.

And treat the vendor's headline claims as claims: the 20% AOV increase and the 40,000+ brands are Logbase's own figures on its own site, with no methodology attached to either.

pricing.notes:
(prices read 2026-09-19 on apps.shopify.com/upsell-cross-sell-kit-1 and on logbase.io/products/shopify-upsell-app-selleasy; re-verified 2026-10-20 on logbase.io/selleasy/pricing) Billed in USD. The App Store listing shows one ladder, Starter, and it is priced by your store's total monthly order count rather than by anything the app does: free up to 50 orders a month, $9 from 51 to 500, $19 from 501 to 1,000, and $29 above 1,000. All four steps carry the same 18 upsell and cross-sell strategies, 50 free AI recommendations, free setup on a call and chat, email and Zoom support, with a 30-day free trial on the paid steps.

Logbase's own pricing page adds two tiers the listing does not show. Pro is $49 a month or $499 a year — $42 a month, which the site says saves $89 — and lifts the order limit entirely while adding 1,000 AI recommendations a month, an AI campaign optimizer, checkout upsells for Shopify Plus, advanced campaign targeting and metafield bulk recommendations. Max is $99 a month or $1,009 a year — $84 a month, saving $179 — adding 2,500 AI recommendations a month, advanced customization, a rules engine, an AOV advisor and priority support. An Enterprise tier is quoted on request.

Re-read on 20 October 2026, Logbase's dedicated pricing page at logbase.io/selleasy/pricing carries the same four-step Starter ladder by store orders (free to 50, $9 to 500, $19 to 1,000, $29 above) and the same Pro ($49, or $499 a year) and Max ($99, or $1,009 a year) figures, with a 30-day free trial on any plan and a yearly toggle labelled 15% off, which the figures bear out ($588 against $499, $1,188 against $1,009). The same page also prices Starter a second way: its plan cards and comparison table read 'Starts at $15 per month', or $153 billed yearly. The page does not reconcile the two, so check the charge Shopify shows at install.

compare_with.name: UpsellPlus
compare_with.why:
Both cover the same surfaces — product page, cart, checkout, post-purchase — so the difference that matters is what you are billed for. UpsellPlus meters the upsell revenue the app is allowed to generate for you, and that meter does not stop where the pricing page appears to: $500 a month on free and on its $49 plan, $2,000 at $119, then a Scale ladder that runs $199 up to $5,000, $299 up to $10,000, $399 up to $15,000, $499 up to $20,000, $699 up to $30,000, $799 up to $40,000 and $999 with no ceiling. Only the $199 step is published; UpsellPlus support confirmed the rest in writing on 21 September 2026, and a store that passes $5,000 is moved to the $299 tier automatically, so the bill rises by itself.

Selleasy meters your store's total orders instead and never touches the revenue: nothing under 50 orders a month, $29 above 1,000, with the same features at every step. That makes the two apps diverge hardest exactly where an upsell app is working — at $20,000 of upsell revenue a month UpsellPlus is $499 and Selleasy is still $29, while a quiet 5,000-order store pays $29 to Selleasy and $0 to UpsellPlus. Run your own upsell revenue and your own order count through both before you choose; they are not comparable on the entry price.

Check the Plus question on both. On UpsellPlus their FAQ says Shopify Plus is required only for checkout customization and checkout upsells, which is Shopify's restriction rather than theirs — cart, product page, drawer, thank-you and post-purchase offers work without it. On Selleasy the checkout upsells sit on the $49 Pro tier that the App Store listing does not show at all.
